messages:
Carmen Rivera: Quick question — when we do soft-retries at the edge, should we include a request fingerprint in the retry key to avoid duplicate side-effects?
Alice Chen: probably yes for dedupe, but we need to be careful about PII in fingerprints.
Ben K.: +1 on dedupe. Also: fingerprint granularity? path+method vs include body hash?
Carmen Rivera: Thinking path+method+model+input-hash (sha256 of normalized prompt). Exclude headers and auth.
Diego Morales: watch out for streaming requests — a soft-retry that replays a stream can produce duplicate partial outputs. We can't always rewind the client stream.
Erin Patel: For streaming, we should treat most as non-retriable unless we have an explicit resume token from the model/runtime. Soft-retry OK for short-lived non-streaming RPCs.
Frank Li: Implementation idea: compute fingerprint server-side after normalization, store small entry in a TTL dedupe table keyed by (fingerprint, retry-window, tenant). If retry seen -> return previous response or a 409-like dedupe marker.
Ben K.: What about memory / cardinality for that table? High-traffic routes could blow up.
Alice Chen: TTL like 60s by default, configurable per-route. Also sample eviction + sharded LRU to bound mem. We can surface metrics for collision rate.
Diego Morales: Another option: use probabilistic structures (bloom filter) to reduce mem but then you get false positives which would reject legitimate requests — meh.
Carmen Rivera: Tradeoff table: deterministic table = accurate dedupe but more memory. Prob structure = cheap but possible false dedupe. Need product to choose.
Erin Patel: Also consider privacy: normalized prompt hash must be irreversible and we should strip PII first. Ops/legal needs to sign off on exact normalization.
Frank Li: Header proposal (proto):
```
x-rw-retry-id: <client-provided-uuid>
x-rw-fingerprint: <server-computed-hash, hex>
x-rw-soft-retry: true|false
```
Carmen Rivera: We should prefer server-generated fingerprint (so clients can't game it). Client retry-id still useful for correlating attempts.
Ben K.: How do we handle mixed cases: client sends retry-id but server sees different fingerprint due to normalization differences?
Alice Chen: Log a telemetry event with both values; if mismatch frequency > threshold, increment normalization mismatch alert. We can fallback to conservative non-dedupe for that tenant while we investigate.
Diego Morales: For streaming resumption: if we have model-side resume tokens, we can support retry with exact offset+fingerprint. Without that, we reject soft-retry for that call.
Erin Patel: Operational rollout: behind feature flag per-route. Start canary on internal-only tenants, collect dedupe hit/miss, memory usage, normalization mismatch rate.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: feature=edge-soft-retry-fingerprint on 10% of edge nodes.
Frank Li: Edge behavior pseudo:
```
if (is_streaming && !has_resume_token) {
  return non-retriable;
}
fingerprint = compute(normalized_payload);
if (dedupe_table.exists(fingerprint)) {
  return cached_response;
}
store(dedupe_table, fingerprint, response, ttl=route_ttl);
return response;
```
Carmen Rivera: One more: fallback policy when dedupe table unavailable (eg mem pressure). Should default to safe: no retry/dedupe.
Alice Chen: Agreed. Also expose a per-route knob for TTL and max table size.
Ben K.: Can we reuse existing cache infra (local shard + central metadata) rather than new table? avoids extra components.
Diego Morales: Reuse sounds good if the semantics match (fast writes, short TTL). Need to confirm eviction guarantees.
Erin Patel: I'll draft an RFC addendum with: fingerprint algorithm, normalization steps (PII stripping), header semantics, streaming exceptions, rollout plan, and metrics to collect (dedupe_hits, false_positive_rate, mem_usage, normalization_mismatch).
Carmen Rivera: Awesome. Please tag me when ready. @Erin Patel
Frank Li: I'll prototype server fingerprint code and a small test harness that simulates retries and stream cases.
Ben K.: Cool. If RFC lands this week we can do a limited canary next week.
Carmen Rivera: Thanks everyone — looks like consensus on server-side fingerprint + conservative streaming behavior.
Alice Chen: :+1:
deploy-bot: Canary expansion: feature=edge-soft-retry-fingerprint -> 30% nodes (scheduled).
